Airport security lines: I asked the TSA agent if my toothpaste was still considered a liquid, and he said, "Yes, but now it's a witness."
Endless Zoom meetings: I hate endless Zoom meetings so much, I started using the "breakout rooms" feature just to get a minute of peace.
First dates: You know a first date is going well when you're already planning the exit strategy.
Smart home devices (like a Roomba or Ale: I asked Alexa to play some jazz, and now my house thinks it's a 1920s speakeasy — I keep hearing whispers and the fridge is stealing my wine.
Going to the gym for the first time: I walked into the gym like I was going to a job interview, and the weights looked at me like they already knew I was lying.
Customer service phone menus: I called customer service and the menu asked if I wanted to speak to a representative, but I just wanted to scream into the void — turns out that's option 6.
Trying to eat healthy/Dieting: I tried to eat healthy, but my body is like, "You're not fooling anyone, I still want that pizza."
The behavior of cats vs. dogs: Cats are like exes — they'll knock things off the table, then act like it's the first time they've ever seen a table. Dogs are like your therapist, always there to wag their tail and listen to you cry about the cat.
Self-checkout machines at the grocery st: I tried to return a bag of frozen peas at the self-checkout, but it kept asking if I wanted to "scan the item" — I didn't realize they were offering a career in retail.
Insomnia and trying to fall asleep: I tried counting sheep, but now I'm worried the entire flock is judging me.
Buying things you don't need online: I bought a waffle maker because it said "1000+ ratings" — turns out I was just buying the same person's opinion over and over.
Awkward family gatherings: I asked my uncle if he's seen my cousin, and he said, "Yeah, he's in the bathroom crying because he accidentally liked a Facebook post from his ex." I said, "That's not awkward, that's just basic human drama."
Streaming service algorithms (e.g., Netf: I asked Netflix what I should watch next and it said, "Based on your history, you might like this show about a guy who's really good at guessing what you want to watch."
Coffee shop baristas and complicated ord: I asked for a black coffee and they said, "Sure, but would you like that with a side of judgment?"
Commuting in heavy traffic: I asked the traffic jam if it was ever going to end, and it said, "Not unless you're a really good driver... and I don't think you are."
Job interviews: I asked the interviewer if I could bring my resume in a backpack, and he said, "Sure, but if you're not hired, we're keeping the backpack."
Keeping houseplants alive: I tried to keep a houseplant alive, and now it's the only one in the house that's more responsible than me.
Forgetting passwords: I forgot my password again, so I had to answer my own security questions. Fortunately, I still remember who I am.
High school reunions: You know you're at a high school reunion when the principal's still the only one with a life.
Assembling flat-pack furniture (e.g., IK: I tried to assemble my IKEA bookshelf while drunk, and now it's a modern art installation called "The Anger of a Man Who Can't Read Instructions."
Tech support/Helping parents with techno: My mom asked for help setting up a smart TV, so I walked her through it step by step. Now she's watching Netflix in another room — with the TV on the floor.
Alarm clocks and waking up early: I tried to wake up early to beat the rush, but my alarm clock just stared at me like, "You're already late."
The culture of social media influencers: Social media influencers are like chefs — they make everything look easy, but if you ever actually tried to cook what they eat, you'd realize they're just really good at editing.
Cryptocurrencies or \"Tech Bros\": I don't trust a cryptocurrency that can't buy me a cup of coffee, but I trust a tech bro to convince me that it can.
Going to the dentist: I told my dentist I was afraid of needles, and he said, "Don't worry, we'll just use a big one."
Moving to a new apartment: I told my landlord I was moving out because the showerhead was too strong — he said I was just being hard-headed.
Annoying neighbors: I used to think my neighbor was just loud, until I realized he was trying to teach the squirrels how to play the drums.
Overpacking for a vacation: I overpacked so much that my suitcase started whispering, "I think you're confusing me with a storage unit."
Swiping left on someone's profile is the modern version of saying "nice hat" while walking past a stranger.
Public transportation/Subways: I love public transportation, especially when it's just me and a bunch of strangers silently judging each other's life choices.
Wedding planning: I told my fiancé I wanted a small wedding, and she said, "Okay, just 500 people and a 5-star venue." I said, "That's not small!" She said, "It's small for us."
Autocorrect text message fails: I told my mom I was dating a girl named "Katie," but autocorrect changed it to "Catie" — now she's worried I'm seeing a cat.
Procrastination: I procrastinate so much I have a full-time job just avoiding my other jobs.
Group chats that never stop buzzing: I joined a group chat that's always buzzing, but I'm not sure if it's because everyone's talking or because the app is stuck in a loop of my grandma's cat sneezing.
The cost of living/Being broke: I'm so broke, my bank account is like a GPS — it just says "Recalculating..." and never gives a direction.
Getting a bad haircut: I asked for a simple trim, and the barber gave me a new identity. I don’t even know myself anymore.
Overly complicated modern fitness trends: You know you're living in the future when your workout involves a treadmill, a resistance band, and a spreadsheet.
People who talk at the movie theater: I hate people who talk at the movie theater, but I especially hate the ones who whisper. You know what they're about to say before they say it, and it's always something like, "I think that's the guy from *The Office*."
Cooking disasters: I once tried to make soup and ended up with a science experiment that my cat refused to touch. Turns out, I forgot to add the water.
Small talk about the weather: I asked the weather if it was going to rain today, and it said, "Maybe, but I'm not commitment-oriented."
Modern fashion trends: You know you're living in a modern fashion trend when your jeans are tighter than your ex's personality and your sneakers are more expensive than your car.
Waiting in doctors' offices: Waiting in doctors' offices is like waiting for a text from someone who's never online.
Getting older/Turning 30: I turned 30 and realized my body is just a rental — the lease is up, the maintenance fees are through the roof, and the warranty expired the day I hit 25.
Video game culture: I hate when people say "I don't have time to play video games," like they're not aware that I've been playing them with my eyes closed for 10 years.
Corporate buzzwords (e.g., \"Synergy\"): I tried to use "synergy" in a sentence, but my boss said I was just repeating myself — he didn't want to hear about the "cross-functional team" I was on.
Dealing with landlords: I told my landlord I was going to start a band, he said, "Great, but can you at least pay rent on time? I can't schedule a show with a bunch of guys who can't hold a note and a tenant who can't hold a check."
Astrological signs/Horoscopes: I told my zodiac sign I was breaking up, and it said, "But we're meant to be!" I said, "Yeah, I know, that's why I'm going to find someone who's not on my level."
People who overshare online: I don't trust people who overshare online — they're the reason I now know what your breakfast tasted like, where you got your hair cut, and why you're mad at your ex.
Veganism or extreme dietary restrictions: I tried veganism for a week, then realized my body was just mad about the lack of cheese.
Trying to assemble a tent/Camping: I tried to assemble a tent like it was a puzzle, but now I'm 99% sure the instructions were written in a language that doesn't exist anymore.
